text:
mara: Heads-up — I repro'd a weird perf/oom combo on paged-attn during nightly stress. When seq len spikes briefly (~1k->4k) we see slot saturation + a kernel flip loop that keeps allocating small blocks and never coalesces. stack traces and logs below.

joey: ugh. is this the slab handoff path again? :grimacing:

mara: looks related but not identical. allocator shows many ~4-8KB allocations from pagehouse while blocktable growth stalls. KV pager keeps creating new pages instead of reusing freed slots.

devin: can you paste the allocator trace?

mara: sure — snip of debug dump (trimmed):
```
ALLOC TRACE: requester=paginated_attn kernel=flashv2_paged
  allocate slab=4096 id=0x7f9c... free_slots=2
  allocate slab=8192 id=0x7f9d... free_slots=1
  free slab=4096 id=0x7f9c... free_slots=0
  allocate slab=4096 id=0x7f9e... free_slots=0
  pagehouse: created new page page_id=1123 size=64KB
  blocktable: insert failed -> resize -> new slab allocation
  kernel chooser: candidate=flashv1(optimized) score=0.68 -> switched to paged_kern (fallback)
```

mara: note the chooser flip right after blocktable resize. That triggers different page alignments.

li: do we have telemetry for the chooser decision inputs? seq_len distro, kv_cache_util, inflight_batch_size?

mara: yes: samples show seq_len spike -> batch size jumps -> kv_cache_util goes to 87% -> chooser threshold crossed -> fall back to paged kernel. But the paged kernel alloc path requests many small fixed-size pagehouse blocks that the current slab allocator treats as external allocations (no coalescing).

ana: (typo, should be ana) I ran a microbench earlier that made small allocations churn; results showed fragmentation ratio ~2.1. Could that explain the stall?

devin: fragmentation that high will force pagehouse to create new pages rather than reuse. Do we log free-list lengths?

mara: yes. free-list length for 4KB bin drops to 0 and stays there for ~3s during the spike. So repeated allocate/free churn doesn't refill because freed slabs are being held by inflight kernels in a different arena. Possible concurrency handoff bug.

joey: hmm — could be the slab->pagehouse handoff where we move ownership to the page IO thread. If handoff uses deferred reclaim, quick subsequent allocations won't see freed slots.

mara: exactly. I instrumented timestamps: free called at t=1.243s but reclaim visible at t=1.257s. During that window, kernel chooser has already switched and different alignment is requested -> new page. Multiply that across many workers and we explode page count.

li: what's the impact on latency and GPU utilization?

mara: latency tail spikes 2-3x for affected requests. GPU utilization drops 15% because more host-side paging and IO stalls. Perf regression trace attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/slot-sat-4329

ana: do we see different behavior if we force kernel chooser to prefer flashv1 (non-paged) for those batches?

mara: I forced it in a canary: kernel lock-in avoids the flipping and fragmentation disappears. But flashv1 OOMs for very long seqs, so can't just force globally.

devin: possible fixes: 1) tighten chooser hysteresis (require longer stability before flip), 2) make slab handoff immediate for page-sized frees when inflight quota low, 3) coalesce small pagehouse allocations back into larger slabs.

joey: +1 on chooser hysteresis. We've seen flip-flop instabilities before. Hysteresis could be simple exponential smoothing of seq_len and kv_util and only flip when smoothed metric crosses threshold for >N ms.

li: also add a metric for "chooser flips per minute" and an alarm when >X. We can correlate with page count growth.

mara: I ran a quick patch to extend chooser flip cooldown from 50ms -> 250ms. Canary reduced flips by ~92% and page creations dropped accordingly. Patch diff:
```diff
--- a/runtime/kernel_chooser.cpp
+++ b/runtime/kernel_chooser.cpp
@@
- if (flip_timer.elapsed_ms() > 50) commit_switch();
+ if (flip_timer.elapsed_ms() > 250) commit_switch(); // reduce oscillation under seq spikes
```

mara: note: this is conservative but low-risk. We should also consider improving allocator reclaim path.

ana: agree. For allocator reclaim, a fast-path reclaim for last-freed page if a new allocation requests same bin could avoid many allocations.

devin: can you perf benchmark the canary under our seq-spike harness? If it fixes tail without regress on steady-state, we can ship.

mara: running now — short run (10m) shows tail p99 reduced from 480ms -> 170ms in spike window, overall avg unchanged. I'll run longer.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist start: canary flagged, traffic routed to q/a canary, monitoring enabled.

li: please add telemetry: chooser_decision{from,to}, flip_cooldown_ms, pagehouse_created, free_list_len per bin. Those should be labels or series so alerts easy.

mara: will add metrics and longer benchmark (1h). Also adding a debug view in console to surface recent flips and pagehouse growth per instance.

joey: follow-up: we should also audit kernel alloc alignment requirements. Maybe the paged kernel could request slab-aligned blocks to make reuse possible. Worth a quick design doc?

mara: noted. I'll drop a short RFC in #eng-runtime after the canary results. For now, immediate step: patch chooser hysteresis + telemetry + longer bench + open issue for allocator handoff improvement.

devin: thanks mara. great triage. :clap:

mara: thanks all. I'll update thread with bench results and link to the RFC.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist complete: canary running (10% instances), alerting hooked.
